text:
Olivia Miles broke further records this week as her remarkable start to life in the WNBA continued

Former Notre Dame star Olivia Miles broke Caitlin Clark's record for the most 3-pointers made by a rookie in a single game this week as she dropped 28 points in Minnesota's 87-84 victory over Golden State.

The 23-year-old recorded eight 3-pointers to help steer the Lynx to a sixth successive victory and eighth of the season on Thursday, taking their overall record to 8-2 and Miles' season averages to 17.0 points, 4.9 rebounds, 6.4 assists and 1.5 steals per game.

It means Miles has made history on numerous occasions this season, having already become just the fifth player to record 20+ points and 5+ assists in a WNBA career debut, before becoming just the third player to record at least 10 points and five assists in each of her first three games.

With her latest achievement on Thursday, Miles surpassed Clark and Crystal Robinson's previous rookie record of seven 3-pointers made in a single game, which the former set during the 12th game of her rookie campaign.

Miles has now broken that record in two fewer games, while she also fell just short of breaking one of Paige Bueckers' records.

In 2025, through her first 10 games, Bueckers scored or assisted on 318 of the Dallas Wings' points - the most by any player through 10 games in WNBA history.

Against the Valkyries on Thursday, in Miles' 10th game, the ex-TCU star assisted or scored on 44 of the Lynx's points to bring her season total to 317 - just one point shy of equalling Bueckers' record and two points away from breaking it.

While this is one record Miles will unfortunately have to accept defeat on, there are sure to be plenty more she'll equal or break throughout the course of the season, given the way she has taken to the WNBA like a duck to water.

Just three months ago, the New Jersey native was leading TCU through the NCAA Tournament, where she helped the Horned Frogs reach the Sweet Sixteen before bowing out of the postseason tournament.

Now, she is thriving at the professional level, having made a seamless transition from college basketball, and is firmly in the running to be crowned WNBA Rookie of the Year at season's end.

Miles assisted or scored on 44 of the Lynx's points against the Valkyries on Thursday to bring her season total to 317 after just 10 games

Ironically, Miles would set a new precedent should that be the case, as the past four WNBA Rookie of the Year award winners all went first overall during their respective drafts. Miles went second overall in 2026.

Next up for Miles and the Lynx are two more home games against the Seattle Storm (Jun. 6) and Dallas Wings (Jun. 9) at Target Center, where fans will be keen to see whether Minnesota's newest star can continue her stunning start to life in the WNBA.

Elsewhere, Indiana Fever reporter Scott Agness claims he lost his WNBA press credentials after a dispute over his Clark reporting, amid her suspicious recent absence.
